literal.prompt: Как называют эффект, при котором плавучий шельф замедляет течение ледников с суши?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The AAP defines ice shelves as floating extensions and states they have a buttressing effect that slows inland ice discharge via glaciers (L302,L306). NSIDC describes the shelf/glacier back-pressure system (L73,L116). Alternative labels are distinct technical mechanisms; the key is the shelf buttressing effect.
literalGroups.locator: AAP L302,L306; NSIDC Ice Shelf L71,L73,L116.

literalGroups.literal: Это подпирающее действие шельфового ледника. При разрушении шельфа наземные ледники могут ускориться, хотя сам плавучий лёд почти не повышал уровень моря.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AAP states that ice shelves slow inland ice discharge and that retreat/collapse can lead to more rapid continental-ice discharge; floating shelf calving does not significantly affect sea level (L306,L309). NSIDC independently records glacier acceleration after shelf collapse (L116).
literalGroups.locator: AAP L306,L309; NSIDC Ice Shelf L116.

literalGroups.literal: Неустойчивость морского щита возможна там, где ложе ниже моря углубляется в сторону материка.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NASA JPL describes the below-sea-level bed and downward inland slope, and how grounding-line retreat can trigger the feedback; the National Academies explicitly names MISI as susceptible to inland-deepening retrograde beds and explains the feedback (L29-L30; L383-L384).
literalGroups.locator: NASA JPL L19-L30; National Academies chapter 3 L383-L384.

literalGroups.literal: Базальное таяние происходит снизу, когда океаническая вода передаёт тепло основанию шельфового ледника.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AAP describes basal melting as loss beneath a shelf where it interacts with ocean water (L315,L328); NSIDC describes warm water thinning from beneath and basal melting (L109-L110).
literalGroups.locator: AAP L315,L328; NSIDC Ice Shelf L109-L110.

literalGroups.literal: Шельфовый ледник тормозит сток наземного льда, передавая сопротивление от боковых берегов и мелей.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AAP states the buttressing effect slows inland ice discharge and changes in shelf shape/size affect associated glacier flow (L306). NSIDC says shelves are supported by peninsulas/islands, balances outflow with backpressure (L71,L73), and loss removes back stress from ice rises and marginal shear areas (L116).
literalGroups.locator: AAP L306; NSIDC Ice Shelf L71,L73,L116.

literalGroups.literal: Гляциоизостатический подъём — медленное поднятие земной коры после уменьшения ледовой нагрузки.
literalGroups.primaryGround: UNRESOLVED: no complete source body was returned for the GIA primary/alternative URLs. The two successful claim contexts above do not define crustal rebound after ice-load reduction. Search-result snippets are not accepted as evidence.
literalGroups.locator: USGS primary and official alternative web.open attempts both returned Internal Error.

correctNoteNewFact.newFact: Backpressure from peninsulas/islands and marginal shear areas contributes resistance to glacier outflow; the current note names lateral support and pinning areas.
correctNoteNewFact.whyNew: The prompt and key state only that a floating shelf slows inland-glacier flow; the note identifies where the backpressure/resistance comes from.
correctNoteNewFact.locator: AAP L306; NSIDC Ice Shelf L71,L73,L116.

entries.absoluteDifficulty: HARD: the correct label requires the specialized glaciological concept of buttressing/backpressure and differentiating it from basal melt, marine ice-sheet instability, and isostatic rebound. These are technical mechanisms/effects, not broad adult knowledge. Editorial judgment, not audience statistics.
